title: Mozzarella in Carrozza
subtitle: Fried mozzarella sandwiches, Neapolitan street food
excerpt: Mozzarella in carrozza is a fried sandwich of white bread and melted mozzarella, dipped in egg and breadcrumbs and cooked in olive oil. The cheese melts completely inside and pulls in strings when you cut it. Eat immediately; it does not hold.
sourceNotes: Mozzarella in carrozza (mozzarella in a carriage) is a Neapolitan street food made from yesterday's bread and mozzarella. It was a way to use up stale bread and slightly old mozzarella, fried in olive oil. The dish appears in Neapolitan cookbooks from the 19th century and remains a popular street snack in Naples and Campania.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble and press the sandwiches, then refrigerate for 30 minutes before dipping and frying. Cold sandwiches hold together better when fried.

content.text: Mozzarella in carrozza is a fried cheese sandwich: thick-cut white bread, a generous layer of mozzarella, dipped in egg and breadcrumbs, and fried in olive oil until the crust is golden and the cheese inside has melted. The name means mozzarella in a carriage, which describes the bread enclosing the cheese on all sides. It is Neapolitan street food and a very good thing to do with yesterday's bread and leftover mozzarella.

items.prepNote: crusts removed, each about 1.5 cm thick
fresh, sliced about 8 mm thick and drained on kitchen paper

content.text: Lay 4 slices of bread on a work surface. Divide the mozzarella among them, keeping it well within the edges. Top with the remaining bread slices and press down firmly.
Refrigerate the sandwiches for 30 minutes so they firm up. This helps them hold together during coating and frying.
Set up three shallow bowls: one with flour, one with the beaten eggs (seasoned with salt), one with breadcrumbs.
Coat each sandwich in flour, shaking off the excess. Dip in beaten egg, letting any excess drip off. Press into the breadcrumbs to coat all sides evenly.
Heat the sunflower oil in a deep frying pan to 175°C. Fry the sandwiches two at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden. The mozzarella should be fully melted inside.
Drain on kitchen paper for 30 seconds and eat immediately. The cheese sets quickly and the crunch fades.

Mozzarella in carrozza is Neapolitan, made as a way to use up mozzarella that was no longer fresh enough to eat raw and bread from the day before. Both ingredients fry well even when slightly past their best. The dish is still sold from street vendors and market stalls in Naples. Some versions include anchovies inside the sandwich, which adds salt and depth and is worth trying.
